title: KGF session receipt (kgfq C6, D5, D17; kgf-explorer D5)
description: What makes an approximate answer a finding. A table carries its receipt in its Parquet footer under `kgf.receipt`, which is the receipt of record; a step that wrote no table carries it in its log record. Shared by the clients that write sessions (notes/session-format.md §5): `core` is read the same way by every client, and `detail` belongs to the operation named by `core.kind`. A reader that does not implement that operation keeps `detail` as it came. Unknown fields anywhere are ignored, never refused, so nothing here is closed but the major version: a reader accepts its own major and any minor.

kind.description: The operation that wrote the receipt, by its registry name (docs/session/operations.yaml).

step.description: The log step that produced it.

grade.description: How far the table can be checked later (kgfq D17). `bundle`: read from a KGF release, re-fetched identically by digest. `sparql`: a live endpoint, re-run and compared. `external`: brought in from elsewhere, checked only against the archived copy. `asserted`: typed by a person or a model. A derived table takes the lowest grade among its inputs. Today's values, weakest last: bundle, sparql, external, asserted.

sources.description: Every graph or endpoint the step read, each graded. A `kgf` source is a graph at a pinned release; its digest is its identity and its origin is where it was fetched.

table.description: The table's name, unique in its session.

shape.description: The table's layout; null for a receipt with no table. `bindings`: four columns per variable, the value then its `_kind` (`iri`, `literal`, `bnode`), `_lang` and `_datatype`. `triples`: `s`, `p`, `o` and the object's three companions. No reader infers a layout from the columns.

pattern.description: For a `bindings` table that answers one pattern: each of `s`, `p`, `o` as a term in doc 03 §3.3 syntax or the `?variable` whose columns hold it. Substituting a row's values gives the triple the row stands for.

content_hash.description: `sha256:` and the hex digest of the table's rows in the `kgf.table-hash/1` encoding (notes/session-format.md §5): independent of row order, and the same from any client.

completeness.description: A table is incomplete only when its read left rows the source still had. `incomplete_because` names why: `max_rows`, a budget, a truncation whose cursor was not followed, `error`.

truncation_reasons.description: Every reason a response gave, continued or not: the trace.

bytes_wire.description: Null where the client cannot see the wire.

requests.description: One entry per response. Absent where the list is kept elsewhere and `detail` points at it, as a SPARQL run's is in the engine's own receipt.

continued.description: The client followed this response's cursor.

stopped.description: The read ended here with rows left, and why.

rows.description: Rows of the table this response carried; null for a request that carried none.

bindings.description: For a bound step: how many input tuples were sent and how many found nothing, with a sample of those (kgfq C6's unmatched report, kgf-explorer D8).

inputs.description: Each value, file or table the step consumed, classified against earlier steps' outputs; for a derived table, the receipts' cores of the tables it read, one hop.

detail.description: The operation's own record. kgfq's `fetch`: `intent` and `plan` (kgfq.plan/1). kgfq's `sparql`: `query`, `original_query`, `normalizations`, `lint`, `engine`, `budget`, `outcome`, `statistics`, `requests_by_shape`, and `engine_receipt`, a pointer by path and sha256 to the receipt kgf-sparql wrote.
